title: Setup: Reusing the Parent's Similarity API over a Commutative Ring
content: The file opens the parent namespace CramersRuleOQ05, reusing its conj U N := U N U⁻¹, the relation IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = conj U M, and reflexivity IsSimilar.refl. It fixes a finite decidable index type n and a commutative ring R. Retaining CommRing (rather than a field) is what keeps every result below valid over ℤ and polynomial rings, where the only invertible object needed is the conjugating unit U.
mathContext: Matrices $M \in \mathrm{Mat}_n(R)$ over a commutative ring $R$, with units $U \in (\mathrm{Mat}_n(R))^\times$. Similarity: $M \sim N \iff \exists U,\ N = U M U^{-1}$.

title: Symmetry: Conjugate Back by the Inverse Unit
content: IsSimilar.symm destructures the witness N = U M U⁻¹ and supplies U⁻¹ as the new conjugator, since M = U⁻¹ N U. The proof rewrites (U⁻¹)⁻¹ = U (inv_inv) and cancels using U⁻¹ U = 1, so U⁻¹ (U M U⁻¹) U = M. Symmetry is exactly inversion in the unit group (Matrix n n R)ˣ.
mathContext: If $N = UMU^{-1}$ then $M = U^{-1} N (U^{-1})^{-1} = U^{-1} N U$, so $N \sim M$ via the unit $U^{-1}$.

title: Transitivity and the Bundled Equivalence Relation
content: IsSimilar.trans composes two changes of basis: from N = U M U⁻¹ and P = V N V⁻¹ it produces P = (V U) M (V U)⁻¹, using the unit-group identity (V U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹ V⁻¹ (mul_inv_rev) and then associativity. isSimilar_equivalence bundles reflexivity (from the parent), symmetry, and transitivity into an Equivalence, and isSimilarSetoid packages it as a Setoid — the formal object that makes 'similarity class' well defined.
mathContext: $(VU)^{-1} = U^{-1}V^{-1}$, so $V(UMU^{-1})V^{-1} = (VU)M(VU)^{-1}$; composing transition matrices multiplies them.

title: Conjugation as an R-Algebra Automorphism
content: conjAlgEquiv U upgrades the bare function conj U to a full R-algebra automorphism Matrix n n R ≃ₐ[R] Matrix n n R with inverse A ↦ U⁻¹ A U. The AlgEquiv obligations are discharged by matrix associativity and U U⁻¹ = 1: map_mul' uses U⁻¹ U = 1 to cancel the middle factors, map_add' is bilinearity, and commutes' slides a scalar matrix past U via Algebra.commutes. conjAlgEquiv_apply certifies it agrees definitionally with the parent's conj U. This structural upgrade — from bijection to algebra isomorphism — is what powers the preservation theorem.
mathContext: $\mathrm{conjAlgEquiv}_U : A \mapsto U A U^{-1}$ is an $R$-algebra automorphism of $\mathrm{Mat}_n(R)$; scalars are central, so $U(cI)U^{-1} = cI$.

title: Polynomial Evaluation Preserves Similarity
content: IsSimilar.aeval is the conceptual payoff: if M ~ N then p(M) ~ p(N) for every polynomial p ∈ R[X], via the same unit U. The one-line reason is that evaluation commutes with any algebra homomorphism (Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply), so p(U M U⁻¹) = U p(M) U⁻¹. This is strictly stronger than invariance of any single quantity: the whole commutative subalgebra R[M] is transported by the change of basis. IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval composes with the parent's charpoly_eq to give equal characteristic polynomials for p(M) and p(N).
mathContext: For $\varphi$ an algebra hom, $\varphi(p(x)) = p(\varphi(x))$; with $\varphi = \mathrm{conjAlgEquiv}_U$ this gives $p(UMU^{-1}) = U\,p(M)\,U^{-1}$.

title: Corollary: Powers Preserve Similarity
content: IsSimilar.pow specializes IsSimilar.aeval to p = X^k (using map_pow and aeval_X) to conclude M^k ~ N^k. This recovers the familiar fact that conjugation commutes with taking powers, now as an instance of the general polynomial-preservation principle rather than a separate induction.
mathContext: With $p = X^k$, $\mathrm{aeval}(M)(X^k) = M^k$, so $M \sim N \implies M^k \sim N^k$.
